Visual storyboard · script · art direction

MATTE BLACK.
Power in its purest form.

A scene-by-scene visual breakdown of the KOHLER Matte Black Series advertisement. The film contrasts raw landscapes and athletic movement with precise black shower hardware, then resolves into a calm luxury bathroom and brand signature.

12 scene beatsFrames from supplied videoColor & lighting mood boardProposed VO clearly labeled
01 / Overview

Creative intent

Use the film’s own visual contrast as the storytelling engine: rugged and kinetic imagery gives meaning to the still, engineered geometry of the product.

Core idea

Raw energy, controlled by design

The ad does not rely on conventional product explanation. It creates an emotional world from cracked ground, storm clouds, tactile materials, a performer in motion and galloping horses. The matte-black finish becomes the common visual thread: quiet, strong, sculptural and precise. Water then demonstrates the product’s functional payoff; the final bathroom shows the range in context.

Story rhythm

From environment to object to lifestyle

01—08s: Establish drama and reveal the finish.
08—20s: Use human movement and natural textures to build metaphor, then demonstrate water.
20—29s: Present the shower system, campaign line, product details and Matte Black title.
29—32.7s: Resolve into the finished interior and KOHLER logo.

Copy distinction: “MATTE BLACK”, “Capture the powerful drama” and KOHLER are observed in the supplied frames. All voiceover lines in this document are suggested creative options, not a verified transcription of the original soundtrack.

04 / Mood board

Color, material & lighting

Palette is intentionally cool and restrained. The black finish should read as matte rather than glossy; brightness belongs in the water, pale stone, atmospheric haze and controlled rim lights.

INK BLACK#111214Hero product / logo card
MATTE GRAPHITE#282A2CBackgrounds and shadow detail
GUNMETAL#4A4D50Low-sheen edge reflections
STORM GREY#7C8184Weather and concrete textures
CLOUD SILVER#BEC2C4Water highlights / negative space
PALE CONCRETE#D9D9D5Product backdrop
MARBLE IVORY#F0EEE8Finished bathroom
SOFT WHITE#FAFAF7Typography and end-card logo
01 / ELEMENTAL WORLD

Cracked earth, storm and raw surfaces

Use desaturated landscape texture to communicate drama and resilience; keep detail contrast strong but avoid over-sharpened grit.

02 / CAMPAIGN ENERGY

Wild movement and centered typography

Black silhouettes against a lighter horizon create energy while the white type stays restrained and legible.

03 / PRODUCT SILHOUETTE

Round showerhead, clean geometry

Protect the circular outline and nozzle pattern. A pale, low-detail wall gives the black product a clear silhouette.

04 / WATER & REFLECTION

Dense spray, silver highlights

Backlight the water to create a bright edge around the dark fixture; retain tonal detail in the spray.

05 / CONTROL DETAILS

Vertical bars and rounded rectangles

Repeat the product’s vertical and horizontal geometry in the framing. Avoid glossy reflections that make matte black look chrome.

06 / FINISHED INTERIOR

Pale stone with dark fixtures

Use the contrast between light marble / concrete and matte-black hardware. Let the bathroom architecture remain calm and uncluttered.

05 / Art direction

How to reproduce the look

Practical direction for photography, rendering, compositing and sound design.

Product finish

Matte black, not black mirror

Use a dark, low-sheen material with broad soft reflections and a very narrow edge highlight. Preserve subtle separation between the body, spray nozzles and the wall behind it. Avoid glossy wet reflections over the entire product.

Lighting

Shape the product with light, not brightness

Use a large soft key for the body, a narrow grazing strip on one edge and a controlled backlight for water. Keep the black level rich without crushing the contour or nozzle details.

Camera language

Macro precision against cinematic wides

Alternate tight, nearly abstract details with wide landscape / performer imagery. Product shots benefit from centered or architectural alignment; human/action shots can carry more movement and asymmetry.

Editing

Match shapes, direction and texture

Cut circles and rings against showerhead geometry; pair cracked terrain with product texture; match horizontal controls with the motion of the horses. Use dips to black sparingly before copy and the end card.

Environment

Let stone stay quiet

Concrete, dark masonry and pale veined stone support the contrast. Keep bathroom styling uncluttered so the black fixtures remain the clearest graphic elements.

Typography

Few words, confident spacing

Use uppercase white sans-serif lettering with generous tracking, centered or carefully aligned. Keep copy short and give it negative space; don’t animate more than needed.

A tactile braided / ring macro cuts to turbulent cloud and a boot touching cracked ground. These analogies make the finish feel rugged and physical, rather than merely decorative.
